name: EU AI Act: High-Risk AI System Requirements
description: Strict tier. Controls cite Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 by article and paragraph, verified against the authenticated OJ text (CELEX 32024R1689). Articles 9 to 15 and 26 are Chapter III high-risk obligations; Article 50 is a Chapter IV transparency obligation that applies to certain AI systems regardless of high-risk classification, so the ART-50 control set is in scope of this pack by subject, not by the high-risk trigger.

applicability.note: Chapter III high-risk obligations (Articles 9 to 15 and 26), as AMENDED. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI, OJ 24.7.2026, act of 8 July 2026, in force 27 July 2026), Article 1 point (40)(b), replaces the third paragraph point (c) of Article 113 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 with: "Chapter III, Sections 1, 2, and 3, with the exception of Article 6(5), shall apply from: (i) 2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III; and (ii) 2 August 2028 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(1) and Annex I." Read verbatim from the EUR-Lex primary text of the AMENDING regulation, which is why this is verified:true. THE EARLIER OF THE TWO DATES IS USED DELIBERATELY. A pack cannot tell whether a scanned workload is Annex III or Annex I high-risk -- an agent manifest asserts neither -- so one of the two dates has to be chosen. 2 December 2027 means an Annex I system is reported in force eight months before it actually is, which OVER-reports exposure. 2 August 2028 would under-report it for every Annex III system for eight months, erasing priced exposure that genuinely exists. Over-reporting is the cheaper error and is the only one a reader can catch. WHAT IS NOT VERIFIED: no CONSOLIDATED text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 incorporating the omnibus was read, and 2026/1744 carries 43 amendment items of which only point (40) was inspected individually, so another date-bearing amendment cannot be ruled out. The omnibus does NOT touch Article 113 third paragraph point (b), so the 2 August 2025 penalty date below stands unamended. PENALTIES ARE A DIFFERENT DATE AND A DIFFERENT CHAPTER. Article 113, third paragraph, point (b) of Reg. 2024/1689: "Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII and Chapter XII and Article 78 shall apply from 2 August 2025, with the exception of Article 101." Chapter XII is Penalties, so Article 99 applies from 2 August 2025 -- but ARTICLE 101 IS EXPRESSLY EXCEPTED and falls to the general 2 August 2026 date. A claim that "Arts 99 and 101 apply from 2 Aug 2025" is half wrong and must be written as "Art. 99 (Art. 101 excepted)". No check in this pack evidences a penalty provision, so no window here is set to that date.

controlSets.name: ART-9 Risk Management System
controlSets.description: Article 9(2) lists the steps of the risk management system: (a) identification and analysis of risks, (b) estimation and evaluation, (c) evaluation against post-market monitoring data, (d) adoption of appropriate and targeted risk management measures. The two workload checks here are measures, so they sit under 9(2)(d), not 9(2)(a). Article 9 mandates no named technical control; these are proxies for a documented measure, and the cybersecurity obligation they most directly serve is Article 15(5).

controls.name: ART-9(2)(d) Adoption of Risk Management Measures
controls.description: Verified against Article 9(2)(d), 'the adoption of appropriate and targeted risk management measures designed to address the risks identified pursuant to point (a)'. Running non-root and refusing privilege escalation are two such measures. Proxy: the Regulation requires that measures be adopted and documented, not these measures.

checks.name: AI system container runs as non-root
checks.description: No container may run as UID 0. An explicit runAsNonRoot: false or runAsUser: 0 is fatal at pod level and at container level; otherwise a container without its own runAsNonRoot inherits the pod value. Pod Security Admission restricted rejects a pod that sets runAsNonRoot: false at pod level even where every container overrides it to true, so a pass here means the pod is admissible, not merely that it would run non-root.
checks.celExpression: has(object.spec) && has(object.spec.containers) && size(object.spec.containers) > 0 && !(has(object.spec.securityContext) && has(object.spec.securityContext.runAsUser) && object.spec.securityContext.runAsUser == 0) && !(has(object.spec.securityContext) && has(object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot) && object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot == false) && (object.spec.containers + (has(object.spec.initContainers) ? object.spec.initContainers : []) + (has(object.spec.ephemeralContainers) ? object.spec.ephemeralContainers : [])).all(c, ((has(c.securityContext) && has(c.securityContext.runAsNonRoot)) ? c.securityContext.runAsNonRoot == true : (has(object.spec.securityContext) && has(object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot) && object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot == true)) && !(has(c.securityContext) && has(c.securityContext.runAsUser) && c.securityContext.runAsUser == 0) && !(has(c.securityContext) && has(c.securityContext.runAsNonRoot) && c.securityContext.runAsNonRoot == false))
checks.remediation: Configure securityContext.runAsNonRoot to true in all container specifications.

checks.name: No privilege escalation in AI workloads
checks.description: Every container, init container and ephemeral container must set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false. Windows pods are exempt, as they are under Pod Security Admission: the field is a Linux-only field and a Windows pod cannot set it, so demanding it would make a conformant Windows workload impossible to satisfy.
checks.celExpression: has(object.spec) && has(object.spec.containers) && size(object.spec.containers) > 0 && ((has(object.spec.os) && has(object.spec.os.name) && object.spec.os.name == 'windows') || (object.spec.containers + (has(object.spec.initContainers) ? object.spec.initContainers : []) + (has(object.spec.ephemeralContainers) ? object.spec.ephemeralContainers : [])).all(c, has(c.securityContext) && has(c.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation) && c.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation == false))
checks.remediation: Set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation to false in pod specifications.

controlSets.name: ART-10 Data and Data Governance
controlSets.description: Article 10(2) requires data governance and management practices for training, validation and testing data sets, concerning in particular (b) 'data collection processes and the origin of data, and in the case of personal data, the original purpose of the data collection'. That is the provenance obligation.

controls.name: ART-10(2)(b) Data Collection Processes and Origin of Data
controls.description: Verified against Article 10(2)(b). The check reads a single declared boolean, so it is a declaration that the practice exists, not evidence of the practice.

checks.name: Training data provenance and validation
checks.description: Validates that training and validation data sets have verified provenance records.
checks.remediation: Attach verified data provenance metadata and validation certificates to agent definition.

controlSets.name: ART-11 Technical Documentation
controlSets.description: Article 11(1): the technical documentation shall be drawn up before the system is placed on the market, kept up to date, and 'shall contain, at a minimum, the elements set out in Annex IV'. Annex IV is titled 'Technical documentation referred to in Article 11(1)'.

checks.name: Annex IV Technical Documentation Compliance
checks.description: Requires comprehensive Annex IV technical documentation prior to deployment.
checks.remediation: Publish Annex IV technical documentation manifest in the agent governance registry.

controlSets.name: ART-12 Record-Keeping
controlSets.description: Article 12(1): 'High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.' Deployer-side log retention of at least six months is a separate obligation under Article 26(6) and is not checked here.

checks.name: Automatic logging of operational events
checks.description: Ensures autonomous agent operations and decisions are logged automatically to an immutable audit sink.
checks.remediation: Enable automated event logging with immutable telemetry forwarding in agent config.

controlSets.name: ART-13 Transparency and Provision of Information to Deployers
controlSets.description: Article 13(1) is a design obligation: operation must be sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret the output. The instructions-for-use obligation this control checks is Article 13(2) ('shall be accompanied by instructions for use ... concise, complete, correct and clear'), with the mandatory contents listed in Article 13(3).

controls.name: ART-13(2) Instructions for Use Accompany the System
controls.description: Corrected citation: was claimed as Article 13(1), which is the design-transparency obligation and says nothing about instructions. The obligation the check tests is Article 13(2). The check reads a declared boolean, so it is a declaration that instructions exist, not a test of their Article 13(3) contents.

checks.name: Operator transparency and instruction manual
checks.description: Mandates clear operational characteristics, intended purpose, and limitations documentation.
checks.remediation: Provide accessible model transparency card and operator instruction manual.

controlSets.name: ART-14 Human Oversight
controlSets.description: Article 14(4)(a)-(e) lists what the oversight person must be enabled to do: understand capacities and limitations, remain aware of automation bias, interpret output correctly, decide not to use or to disregard, override or reverse the output, and intervene or interrupt through a stop button. Article 14 contains NO general requirement for ex-ante human authorisation of an action. The nearest such requirement is Article 14(5), and it is scoped to the systems in point 1(a) of Annex III (remote biometric identification), where no action may be taken unless the identification has been separately verified by at least two natural persons.

controls.name: ART-14(4) Human Oversight Enablement
controls.description: Proxy, stated as such. The check gates exec, write_file and modify_iam on a valid human_approval_svid claim, which is ex-ante authorisation. Article 14(4)(d)-(e) requires that a person be ABLE to disregard, override, reverse or interrupt; it does not require prior approval. A pre-authorisation gate is a stricter design that satisfies the spirit of 14(4) and is not the letter of any paragraph of Article 14 outside 14(5)'s biometric scope. Do not represent a pass as evidence of Article 14(5) compliance.

checks.name: Privileged action human authorization SVID
checks.description: Mandates human approval credential for sensitive host execution or IAM modification actions.
checks.celExpression: has(request.tool_call) && has(request.tool_call.action) && request.tool_call.action in ['exec', 'write_file', 'modify_iam'] ? (has(request.context) && has(request.context.claims) && request.context.claims.exists(c, has(c.type) && has(c.valid) && c.type == 'human_approval_svid' && c.valid == true)) : true
checks.remediation: Obtain valid human approval SVID prior to executing privileged host operations.

controlSets.name: ART-15 Accuracy, Robustness and Cybersecurity
controlSets.description: Two distinct paragraphs, previously conflated under one control labelled 'ART-15(4) Cybersecurity Measures'. Article 15(4) is robustness: systems 'shall be as resilient as possible regarding errors, faults or inconsistencies', achievable 'through technical redundancy solutions, which may include backup or fail-safe plans'. Article 15(5) is cybersecurity: systems 'shall be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities', with named AI-specific measures against data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, model evasion and confidentiality attacks.

controls.name: ART-15(4) Resilience to Errors, Faults and Inconsistencies
controls.description: Verified against Article 15(4). Bounding cpu and memory is a resilience measure: an unbounded container is the fault mode 15(4) asks to be resilient to. Proxy: 15(4) names no specific control and offers redundancy and fail-safe plans as the examples.

checks.name: CPU and memory limits defined
checks.description: Every container and init container must bound both cpu and memory in resources.limits. Ephemeral containers are excluded: the Kubernetes EphemeralContainer schema forbids resources on them.
checks.celExpression: has(object.spec) && has(object.spec.containers) && size(object.spec.containers) > 0 && (object.spec.containers + (has(object.spec.initContainers) ? object.spec.initContainers : [])).all(c, has(c.resources) && has(c.resources.limits) && 'cpu' in c.resources.limits && 'memory' in c.resources.limits)
checks.remediation: Specify CPU and memory limits in container resource specifications.

controls.name: ART-15(5) Resilience Against Unauthorised Third Parties
controls.description: Corrected citation: the cybersecurity obligation is Article 15(5), not 15(4). Dropping all Linux capabilities reduces what an attacker who alters the system's use can reach, which is squarely 15(5). Proxy: 15(5) names data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, model evasion and confidentiality attacks, none of which a pod spec can evidence.

checks.name: Drop all capabilities for AI workloads
checks.description: Every container, init container and ephemeral container must drop ALL capabilities AND add back nothing outside NET_BIND_SERVICE. Pod Security Admission restricted is a conjunction over both halves; checking only the drop half reports a container that drops ALL and re-adds SYS_ADMIN (mount, ptrace, kernel-module loading) as compliant. Windows pods are exempt, as they are under PSA.
checks.celExpression: has(object.spec) && has(object.spec.containers) && size(object.spec.containers) > 0 && ((has(object.spec.os) && has(object.spec.os.name) && object.spec.os.name == 'windows') || (object.spec.containers + (has(object.spec.initContainers) ? object.spec.initContainers : []) + (has(object.spec.ephemeralContainers) ? object.spec.ephemeralContainers : [])).all(c, has(c.securityContext) && has(c.securityContext.capabilities) && has(c.securityContext.capabilities.drop) && c.securityContext.capabilities.drop.exists(d, d == 'ALL') && (!has(c.securityContext.capabilities.add) || c.securityContext.capabilities.add.all(a, a == 'NET_BIND_SERVICE'))))
checks.remediation: Add ALL to securityContext.capabilities.drop in all container definitions.

controlSets.name: ART-26 Obligations of Deployers of High-Risk AI Systems
controlSets.description: Article 26(1) is 'appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure they use such systems in accordance with the instructions for use'. The monitoring obligation is Article 26(5): 'Deployers shall monitor the operation of the high-risk AI system on the basis of the instructions for use'. Assignment of human oversight to competent persons is Article 26(2).

controls.name: ART-26(5) Deployer Monitoring of the Operation
controls.description: Corrected citation: was claimed as Article 26(1), which is about using the system in accordance with the instructions for use, not about monitoring. The obligation the check tests is Article 26(5). The check reads a declared boolean, so it is a declaration that monitoring is in place, not evidence of monitoring.

checks.name: Continuous deployer monitoring system
checks.description: Ensures deployers monitor system operations based on the instructions of use.
checks.remediation: Activate continuous deployer telemetry and health monitoring in platform settings.

controlSets.name: ART-50 Transparency Obligations for Providers and Deployers of Certain AI Systems
controlSets.description: Article 50(1) requires that a natural person interacting with an AI system be informed that they are. Article 50(2) is the marking obligation: providers of AI systems generating synthetic audio, image, video or text 'shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated'. Deep-fake disclosure by deployers is 50(4). Article 50 is in Chapter IV and binds regardless of high-risk classification.

applicability.note: Article 50 is a CHAPTER IV transparency obligation, not a Chapter III high-risk one, so the framework-level window is wrong for this control set by 16 months, and this is exactly why per-controlSet windows exist. Chapter IV is not named in any of the exceptions in the third paragraph of Article 113, so it falls to the general application date in the first paragraph of Article 113 (2 August 2026), and Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 does not move it. UNVERIFIED: the FIRST paragraph of Article 113 was not read verbatim in the pass that produced this window -- only points (b) and (c) of the third paragraph were -- so 2 August 2026 is inferred from Chapter IV being absent from the exception list rather than read directly. Someone must read Article 113 first paragraph and flip this flag. It is inert until then, and since the date is in the past the inert and the verified behaviour coincide today anyway.

controls.name: ART-50(2) Marking of Synthetic Content as Artificially Generated
controls.description: Corrected citation: was claimed as Article 50(1) under the name 'Synthetic Content Marking and AI Disclosure', conflating two paragraphs. Marking is 50(2); informing a person that they are interacting with an AI system is 50(1) and is NOT checked by this pack. The check also passes when agent.model_type is absent, so an undeclared model type is not gated; see AGENT-CONTEXT.md.

checks.name: Synthetic content watermarking and disclosure
checks.description: Verifies that generative AI models mark synthetic outputs in a machine-readable format.
checks.remediation: Enable cryptographic synthetic content watermarking in generative model pipelines.
